Register ID is required when boundary is selected — A boundary column has been filled but the Register ID cell is empty. The Register ID is auto-populated by formula — ensure you have not accidentally cleared it.
At least one boundary must be selected for the register — A Register ID has been entered but no boundary column has a value. Fill at least one boundary column for every register row.
Invalid boundary code — The boundary value entered is not recognised for this campaign. Use only the boundary codes available in the column dropdowns.

Duplicate Register ID found — The same Register ID appears more than once within the sheet. Each register must have a unique ID. If you created multiple registers at the same boundary, overwrite the auto-populated Register ID to make each one unique.
Register ID already exists in the system — This Register ID has already been created in a previous upload. Remove or rename the duplicate row before re-uploading.

Once registers are successfully created, their boundary and project details cannot be changed from this screen. Contact your system administrator for any corrections.

Download the template using the button above and open it in Microsoft Excel or a compatible spreadsheet application. Do not convert the file to CSV before uploading, as the auto-fill formulas in the Register ID column may stop working.

Each row in the template represents one attendance register. Fill in the boundary columns from left to right — for example, State, then District, then the lowest level you want the register created at. You must fill at least one boundary column per row; rows with no boundary filled will be rejected. The register will be created at the lowest boundary level you have filled in.

The Register ID column is auto-populated based on the lowest boundary you enter. You may overwrite this value if you want a custom name, but every Register ID in the sheet must be unique — duplicate IDs will cause an error and the entire upload will be rejected until resolved.

What happens after you upload: Your file will be processed in the background. You will see a status update on this screen once processing is complete. If any rows have errors, you will be able to download a copy of your file with error details noted against each row. Fix the flagged rows and re-upload to complete register creation.

When a user is mapped to a register, their enrollment date is set automatically to the date of mapping — you do not need to fill this column. The enrollment date determines from which day attendance can be marked for that user.

If you need to remove a user from a register, set their Status column to Disabled. This will trigger an immediate de-enrollment, and attendance cannot be marked for that user from that date onwards. If you enter a future date in the De-enrollment Date column instead, the user will remain active until that date and attendance marking will be automatically blocked after it.

If you need to move a user from one register to another, you must first disable them from their current register. Once their status is set to Disabled and the file is uploaded, they can be mapped to a new register, this can be done on the same day.
Register ID is required — A pre-filled Register ID was accidentally cleared. Re-download the template and do not edit any pre-filled cells.
Cannot change de-enrollment date for this register — The de-enrollment date is locked once set. Contact your system administrator if this needs to be changed.
Register ID does not match expected register — A row contains a Register ID from a different template. Re-download the template for this register and re-enter the data.
Register already exists in a different campaign — The register belongs to another campaign and the entire sheet will be rejected. Ensure you have downloaded the template from the correct campaign.

Enrollment date is required to enroll a new attendee or staff — Enrollment Date is mandatory for all new users, and must also be filled if Team Code or De-enrollment Date is entered. Use DD-MM-YYYY or DD/MM/YYYY format.
Invalid date format. Use DD-MM-YYYY or DD/MM/YYYY — A date cell contains an unrecognised format or extra characters. Accepted formats are DD-MM-YYYY and DD/MM/YYYY only.
Date must be between register start and end dates — An Enrollment or De-enrollment Date falls outside the register's valid date range. Check the campaign dates and correct accordingly.
De-enrollment date cannot be before enrollment date — The De-enrollment Date is earlier than the Enrollment Date on the same row. Correct so that de-enrollment is on or after enrollment.

Individual is already actively enrolled in another attendance register — This user must be de-enrolled from their current register before being added here. Once de-enrolled, they can be mapped to this register on the same day.
Cannot change enrollment date for this register — The enrollment date from a user's previous enrollment in this register cannot be modified. Leave it as it was in the original record.

Download the template using the button above. The template will be pre-filled with all users currently created in the system, split across three sheets — Frontline Workers, Attendance Markers, and Attendance Approvers. Always download a fresh copy of the template before filling it, as the user list and available registers may have changed since your last download.
Columns highlighted in grey (User ID, Name, Login ID, Role, Boundary, and Register ID) are locked and must not be edited. Any changes to these columns will cause that row to be rejected on upload.

This template is specific to a single register — the Register ID is already pre-filled for all rows and cannot be changed. If you need to map users to a different register, download the template from that register separately.

`Enrollment Date` is mandatory for all users. It decides from when attendance can be marked in the register. Rows without this date will be skipped and users will not be mapped. Enter the date in DD-MM-YYYY format. The date should be within the campaign duration

De-enrollment date: The De-enrollment Date column is optional. If you enter a future date here, the user will remain active until that date and attendance marking will be automatically blocked from the following day onwards.

If you need to move a user from one register to another, they must be de-enrolled from their current register first. Once de-enrolled, they can be mapped to a new register on any day after their de-enrollment date.

Case when there is no facility data in the system:

Step 1: When there is no facility data in the system, the “List of available facility” template will be empty. For every facility added the user needs to input the Facility Name (must be unique), Facility Type (Warehouse/Health Facility), Facility Status (Temporary/Permanent), Capacity (Number input)

Step 2: To map the facilities to a given boundary the user needs to copy the correct Boundary Code from the “Boundary Data” sheet. If there are more than one boundaries that a facility needs to be mapped to, the user can add all the boundary codes separated by commas

Step 3: For every facility, the user needs to add Active or Inactive for all facilities under the “Facility Usage” column. All the Facilities marked as “Active” will be used in the campaign being created the ones marked “Inactive” will not be used in the campaign being created.
Step 4: Once all the facilities are added the user needs to save the file on their system and upload the file by pressing “Browse in My Files” option.
Case when there is existing facility data in the system:

Step 1: When you open the downloaded facility template, please refer to the List of available Facility sheet. For existing facilities, kindly add entries in the Boundary Code column. You can find the boundary codes in the Boundary Data sheet. If a facility maps to multiple boundaries, please separate the codes with commas.

Step 2: In this step the user will have to add entries in the Facility Usage column with valid entries being either Active or Inactive where the user can set the usage for a facility to Active if the facility is being is used for a campaign or else can be set to Inactive. The inputs in the Facility Usage column need to be added for all entries.

Step 3: For adding new Facilities which are not present in the list of existing facilities, the user needs to input the Facility Name (must be unique), Facility Type (Warehouse/Health Facility), Facility Status (Temporary/Permanent), Capacity (Number input), Boundary Code(from the Boundary Data Sheet) and Facility Usage (Active/Inactive) as explained previously
Step 4: Once all the facilities are added the user needs to save the file on their system and upload the file by pressing “Browse in My Files” option.
